summary: Re-point the two consumers that come first in the recorded T105 cutover order and close both open findings on each. T068 becomes the registry producer with no manifest edge: T063 is removed from its Dependencies and from todo/config.yaml, T105 is deliberately not added because T105 depends on T068, current manifest binding and its integration acceptance move to T105, and the false T060 parameter-schema citation is replaced by T065's immutable parameter schema. T069 consumes T105 instead of T063 everywhere and states the product-run versus rerun-manifest lifecycle boundary explicitly, with acceptance covering a new run, a linked rerun, cancellation and failure, and rejection of legacy or unregistered inputs. Resolved: A0014:T068:remove-manifest-reverse-dependency, A0013:T068:legacy, A0014:T069:consume-registry-bound-manifest, A0013:T069:legacy.
rationale: Owner direction executed inside the CONTRACT layer, inside the two named targets only. T068 (todo/phases/P06-backtesting-and-strategy/T068.md): T063 removed from Dependencies (now T060, T062, T065) and from todo/config.yaml; T105 deliberately not added, because T105 declares T068 as its dependency and the edge would close a T068-T105 cycle; the contract now identifies T068 as the registry producer whose deterministic validation surface the manifest authority T105 consumes, forbids publishing or validating a manifest so no second manifest publisher exists, moves manifest recording and the old-path-unreachability proof to T105, and stops claiming that T060 carries the parameter-schema vocabulary it cites T065's immutable parameter schema instead (closes A0013:T068:legacy). T069 (todo/phases/P06-backtesting-and-strategy/T069.md): T063 replaced by T105 in Dependencies, in todo/config.yaml and in every normative reference; the deliverables state the lifecycle boundary explicitly (T069 alone owns durable run state, progress, failure, cancellation and restart; the T105 artifact rerun stays an artifact operation that acquires no T069 run state unless it is invoked through a new T069 run record; a rerun requested through the product path creates a new durable run linked to the source manifest, which is preserved read-only and never mutated); acceptance covers a new run, a linked rerun that leaves the source manifest byte-identical, the artifact command staying artifact-only, cancellation and failure, and rejection of legacy or unregistered inputs (closes A0013:T069:legacy). Every other obligation, acceptance criterion and Must-not clause of both contracts is preserved or re-pointed rather than weakened: the deterministic registry enumeration and checksum, the no-network/no-Web-entry/no-implementation-read requirement, the import-layer check, the rejection of caller-invented identities and parameters, and T069's queued/running/failed/cancelled/succeeded durability, no-partial-result and no-Web-session clauses are unchanged. Every other recorded impact stays open and untouched, and this amendment says so explicitly: A0013:T063:legacy, A0013:T064:legacy, A0013:T066:legacy, A0013:T067:legacy (the retirement route, which stays impossible while ordinary PLANNED consumers remain), A0013:T071:legacy, A0013:T072:legacy, A0013:T082:legacy, A0013:T084:legacy, A0013:T085:legacy, A0013:T086:legacy, A0013:T091:legacy, A0013:T096:legacy, A0013:T101:legacy, A0013:T102:legacy, A0013:T103:legacy, A0013:T104:legacy, A0014:T073:use-current-evidence-and-candidate, A0014:T083:consume-registry-bound-candidate-lock, A0014:T084:present-current-manifest-provenance, A0014:T087:read-current-manifest-coverage, A0014:T088:reconcile-current-result-checksums, A0014:T096:include-successor-final-evidence, A0014:T101:assemble-panel-from-current-run-manifests and A0014:T102:consume-schema-bound-robustness. T063 keeps the PLANNED consumers T073, T084 and T101 as well as its successor T105, so it cannot be retired here; no superseded_by, status, attempt, evidence, commit or review field was touched, and no document or revision outside the two contracts and their dependency fields was edited.

impact_assessment.intent: No Intent change. This amendment executes the lower-layer follow-through A0014 itself recorded (todo/amendments/A0014/impacts.json, A0014:T068:remove-manifest-reverse-dependency and A0014:T069:consume-registry-bound-manifest) for the two consumers that come first in the cutover order T105's Replacement and migration names. It cites the governing clauses that already exist, G-STRATEGY-REGISTRY-01 (docs/intent/PROJECT_GOALS.md:506, a registered identity for every executable strategy, manifest identity from the registry, unregistered identities rejected) and G-BACKTEST-RUN-01 (docs/intent/PROJECT_GOALS.md:508, product-level run entry with visible run identity, status, progress, failure reason and cancellation), and adds no new goal obligation. intent_revision is untouched.
impact_assessment.specification: No Spec change and no spec_revision change. The edited text rests on clauses that already exist and were verified in the tree: ARCHITECTURE.md section 2.2 assigns robinhood_lp.strategy.registry to T068 (docs/spec/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:153); WEB_CONSOLE.md WEB-PAGE-012 is the console surface that lists registered strategies; ADR-014 fixes the per-pool manifest and dataset binding T069 requests name; T105's own contract fixes the artifact-rerun versus product-run boundary this amendment restates in T069. No specification clause is contradicted, none is duplicated, and none was edited.
impact_assessment.contracts: Exactly two contracts changed, both named targets: todo/phases/P06-backtesting-and-strategy/T068.md and todo/phases/P06-backtesting-and-strategy/T069.md, plus the two corresponding depends_on lists in todo/config.yaml. Each contract keeps its Dependencies, Outcome, Deliverables, Acceptance, Must not and References sections exactly once, and each Dependencies line equals its configured depends_on list. affected_existing_tasks is empty because no other existing contract is left asserting something these two now deny: T105 already records that T069 must consume it and that T068 must cease consuming the manifest, T073/T084/T101 remain recorded A0014 consumers of T063, T087/T088 remain recorded with their own normative T063 references, and T063/T064/T066/T067 remain recorded on the retirement route; this amendment leaves every one of those impacts open rather than duplicating or silently clearing them.
impact_assessment.dependencies: T068 depends_on becomes [T060, T062, T065]: T063 is gone and T105 is deliberately absent because T105 depends on T068. T069 depends_on becomes [T041, T053, T061, T068, T105]: T063 is replaced by its designated successor. Both dependency fields are amendment-owned for a CONTRACT amendment (tools/workflow/core.py:470-483 pops depends_on for the target tasks), the graph stays acyclic by construction, and the plan still validates. Consumer effects, measured: T063 keeps the PLANNED consumers T073, T084 and T101 and its successor T105, so it is not stranded and not retirable here; T068 keeps its consumers T069, T087, T105-T108; T069 keeps T087 and T088, which now reach T105 directly through T069 instead of transitively through a T063 reference. No other task, dependency or revision was touched.
impact_assessment.implementation: No source, test, schema, tool or configuration file outside todo/config.yaml is edited, and no business code is implemented. T068 and T069 are PLANNED at attempt 0, so this change replaces no shipped behaviour; the currently implemented behaviour that T105 retires (the hard-coded five-name set VALID_STRATEGY_KINDS in src/robinhood_lp/reports/manifest.py:118 and the rerun-manifest CLI integration in src/robinhood_lp/__main__.py) remains owned and dispositioned by T105's Replacement and migration section, which requires the old validator to survive only as unreachable history or as an explicitly versioned legacy reader, and requires every current publication path to bind the registry. This amendment avoids two authoritative paths: T068 may expose a deterministic registry validation surface but explicitly may not publish or validate a manifest, and T069's boundary keeps the artifact rerun artifact-only and gives the product path its own durable run record.
impact_assessment.data: No persisted data, artifact or checksum is read, rewritten or migrated by this amendment, and none is created. Historical T063 manifests, reports and checksums stay byte-identical and read-only under T105, which continues to require an explicit legacy marker and forbids rewriting a historical artifact to claim a registry revision it never recorded. The only new data obligation is inside a future T069 implementation: a linked product rerun creates a new durable run record and leaves its source manifest byte-identical, and a legacy pre-registry manifest is not an admissible current run input. Registry records are deterministic and non-secret.
impact_assessment.operations: No running process, deployment, runtime configuration, CLI surface or background job changes. Operationally the amendment preserves every existing clause: registry availability is a prerequisite of the T105 cutover and a missing, unknown or mismatched binding fails before publication; T069 keeps queued, running with progress, failed, cancelled and succeeded states durable across a restart with a reason code, publishes nothing for a cancelled or failed run, and needs no Web session. Ordering for later work is unchanged: T068 delivers the registry, then T105 cuts the manifest over, then the remaining recorded consumers are re-pointed and T063 can be retired.
impact_assessment.security: No new permission, trust boundary, credential or secret surface. T068 keeps its prohibition on importing RPC, storage, signing or presentation code and its deterministic, network-free registry; T069 keeps its prohibition on writing a credential, endpoint alias or key material into a run record and its no-Web-session requirement; neither contract gains execution, approval, promotion or live authority, and registry or manifest binding grants none. No secret, endpoint value or key material was read, printed or written anywhere in this amendment.
impact_assessment.verification: Planning-artifact checks were run read-only in this worktree as investigation, not as task acceptance evidence: python -m tools.workflow validate returns status OK; python -m tools.check_acceptance check reports no findings; python -m tools.check_citations check reports no findings; each contract's Dependencies line equals its configured depends_on list; the two contracts contain no remaining T063 reference; and the only changed paths are the two target contracts and the two dependency lists in todo/config.yaml. The amended contracts' own verification obligations remain intact and are extended, not relaxed: T068 still requires registry-local identity lookup, rejection of unregistered identities and undeclared parameters, deterministic enumeration and checksum, resolvable code provenance and the import-layer check, while manifest integration and old-path unreachability are verified by T105; T069 additionally requires a new run, a linked rerun whose source manifest stays byte-identical, the artifact command acquiring no run state, cancellation and failure publishing nothing, and fail-closed rejection of legacy or unregistered inputs. No test was run as proof of completion and no evidence or approval record was created or altered.
